newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BUTT OUT, BECKHAM A DOUBT FOR UNITED CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BUTT OUT, BECKHAM A DOUBT FOR UNITED CUP CLASH.

text.p: Manchester United's ambition to become the first club ever to reach four successive English F.A. Cup finals were dealt a blow on Friday, 24 hours before their fourth round tie against Wimbledon at Old Trafford.

United, who beat Londoners Tottenham in the last round, will be hoping to send another disappointed side back to the capital on Saturday but manager Alex Ferguson said Nicky Butt would miss the tie and that David Beckham was doubtful.

Beckham has been in outstanding form lately, not only scoring a superb goal direct from a free kick to kill off Tottenham in the third round but also scoring with a 25-metre drive against Spurs in a league match the following week.
And Wimbledon know all about his special goals after he scored against them with his amazing 50-metre shot from inside his own half on the first day of the season.
"David did some running yesterday and took part in a little bit of training but we cut it short because he wasn't 100 percent so we will have to wait to see how he is," Ferguson said.

United will also be without Norwegian centre back Ronny Johnsen (hamstring) and David May (hernia) so 21-year-old Chris Casper will make his F.A. Cup debut, although he has played in the league, League Cup and briefly in the European Champions' League already this season.

United beat Chelsea to win the Cup in 1994, lost the 1995 final to Everton and returned to Wembley last May when they beat Liverpool. In the 126-year history of the competition no club has ever reached four successive finals.
The weekend action has a disjointed look to it as third round matches and third round replays are also being staged.

But there is plenty of potential for upsets, with second division Brentford hosting first division strugglers Manchester City and high-flying third division Carlisle fancying their chances against premier league Sheffield Wednesday.
Minor league Hednesford Town probably lost any chance they might have had of upsetting Middlesbrough when they agreed to switch the match to the north-east.

Hednesford, from the Midlands, had never got past the qualifying rounds in their 109-year history until this season and a win over Bryan Robson's premier league team -- Ravanelli, Juninho et al -- would rank alongside the all-time giant-killing acts.

Woking, another minor league outfit who did create one of the cup's most famous upsets when they knocked out West Bromwich Albion six years ago, will do well to repeat that against Coventry, who have looked an improved side since Gordon Strachan took over from Ron Atkinson even if they have failed to win their last three games.

Besides the Manchester United-Wimbledon tie, there are three other all-premier league matches with Derby playing Aston Villa, and on Sunday Chelsea hosting Liverpool and Newcastle playing Nottingham Forest.
Chelsea and Liverpool were the two sides beaten when United won the Cup in 1994 and l996 and both must fancy their chances of a return to Wembley this season.
Liverpool beat Chelsea 5-1 in September but Chelsea beat Liverpool 1-0 on New Year's Day and the match at Stamford Bridge has the makings of a classic.

Newcastle, who battled to get past Charlton in a third round replay the day after Kenny Dalglish took over from Kevin Keegan, face a Nottingham Forest side rejuvenated since Stuart Pearce took over as temporary player-manager a month ago. The two sides drew 0-0 six weeks ago, a scoreline unlikely to repeated on Sunday.
